findings.title: enableSqlExpressions has dead logic that always returns false
findings.body: The function `enableSqlExpressions` takes `*ExpressionQueryReader` and reads `h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)`, but both branches of the conditional return `false`. The feature toggle is referenced but its value has no effect on the outcome; the function unconditionally returns `false`, making the parameter `h`, the `features` field access, and the conditional dead code. A future maintainer who wants to re-enable SQL expressions by toggling `FlagSqlExpressions` will be misled into thinking the flag works, when in fact the function must be rewritten. The intended behavior could be expressed simply as `return false` (or, if the flag should still control the feature, `return h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)`). Leaving the bogus intermediate variable `enabled` and unreachable branch will confuse future readers and any tooling (linters, dead-code detectors) that flags `h` as unused.

findings.title: Vulnerable SQL-interpolation pattern preserved in dead code
findings.body: The line `cmd := fmt.Sprintf("SELECT json_serialize_sql('%s')", rawSQL)` is the exact vulnerable pattern behind CVE-2024-9264. It builds a DuckDB SQL statement by interpolating user-controlled `rawSQL` after only escaping single quotes (`strings.Replace(rawSQL, "'", "''", -1)`), which is an incomplete sanitizer (e.g. backslash escapes, Unicode, or comment sequences can still break out). It is currently unreachable because the stubbed `RunCommands` returns "not implemented" and because `ReadQuery` blocks SQL queries via `enableSqlExpressions`, but this function and its file are left in place for easy re-enabling. If anyone later swaps the stub back for the real DuckDB backend or removes the `enableSqlExpressions` guard, the original RCE/LFI vulnerability returns with no review trigger. Either delete the entire `pkg/expr/sql/parser.go` body (since it is unreachable) or replace the format-string concatenation with proper DuckDB parameter binding / parser API usage before the code can be re-enabled.

findings.title: Misleading user-facing error message for disabled feature
findings.body: When a user submits a SQL expression query they get `fmt.Errorf("sqlExpressions is not implemented")`. This phrasing suggests the feature simply has not been built yet, which contradicts reality: the feature was shipped, then deliberately disabled because of CVE-2024-9264. Users filing a request to "implement SQL expressions" or assuming it will arrive in a future release is a foreseeable miscommunication. Consider wording such as "sqlExpressions are disabled for security reasons (see CVE-2024-9264)" or, at minimum, "sqlExpressions are not supported in this version" so users understand this is an intentional, security-driven removal and not a missing feature.

findings.title: No automated test verifies the SQL-expressions kill switch
findings.body: The patch is a security mitigation that introduces a new behavior (any `QueryTypeSQL` request must be rejected with "sqlExpressions is not implemented" before any SQL parsing happens, and the `enableSqlExpressions` helper must return `false` unconditionally), yet no test file is modified or added. The PR description relies on a manual verification by one engineer. For a CVE fix this should be covered by an automated unit test in `pkg/expr/reader_test.go` (or equivalent) that asserts: (1) a `QueryTypeSQL` query returns the expected error and never reaches `NewSQLCommand`/`sql.TablesList`, and (2) `enableSqlExpressions` returns `false` regardless of the feature toggle state. Without that test, a future refactor that "restores" the feature-flag branch or accidentally wires `enableSqlExpressions` to `true` will not be caught by CI.
